items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: So when I left Patti I let him know that I was free and I went to work with him right away. And I stayed with him five years.

ctx.x: And I quit. I put my notice in I just couldn't go through that. You know, it was just kind of anticlimatic, you know. Yeah. So I loved her but no. So I -- while I was rehearsing with her Bobby Trumpet asked me to play with him, as a matter of fact I went out to see him at Whitting Hills, and I told him that I would like to play with him but I was committed to Patti. I would prefer playing with him but I had been rehearsing with her and I couldn't. He said, you know, I admire you for being loyal to Patti, he said,…

So when I left Patti I let him know that I was free and I went to work with him right away. And I stayed with him five years. Very -- five years, and it was a very pleasant association. But -- and he was admired as I said by all musicians, black, white, they all loved Bobby, so consequently they would all come in to see Bobby, and to hear me. And I got quite -- it was kind of gratifying and reward-
ing, after having been, you know, in the -- on pension I should say with Nat for so many years.
